description: Climb from Durham's oldest bridge into the fortress world of Prince Bishops, saints and a perfectly preserved Victorian pub.
short_description: Cross medieval arches, conquer Palace Green and finish in 1899.
author: Day Tripping Quiz
transport_note: A short but steep route over cobbles and historic streets. Palace Green is pedestrian-friendly; Hallgarth Street has normal city traffic.

before_you_go.terrain: A short but steep route over cobbles and historic streets. Palace Green is pedestrian-friendly; Hallgarth Street has normal city traffic.
before_you_go.hills: Includes a notable steep section; take your time and use a suitable alternative where available.
before_you_go.steps: No required steps are known, though temporary diversions may vary.
before_you_go.accessibility: Steep gradients and historic surfaces may be difficult; check a step-free alternative before setting off.
before_you_go.toilets: Check local public facilities before setting off; customer toilets may depend on opening hours.
before_you_go.footwear: Supportive, grippy walking shoes are recommended.
before_you_go.dogs: Outdoor route; keep dogs under control and check the final venue’s current dog policy.
before_you_go.pushchairs: Possible but the steep section and historic surfaces may be demanding.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Begin on Durham's oldest crossing, where two shallow arches replaced six lost to a furious Wear.
stops.Hint_1: Find the pedestrian bridge linking Silver Street and Crossgate.
stops.Hint_2: Stand where the castle and cathedral rise together above the River Wear.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Bishop Ranulf Flambard built the first bridge here in 1127. Flooding destroyed it in 1400, and today's Grade I-listed replacement has two visible stone arches; it was widened in 1859.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Climb to a conqueror's stronghold that became a bishop's palace and then a student's home.
stops.Hint_2: Face the castle entrance opposite the cathedral.
stops.Unlock_Fact: William the Conqueror ordered Durham Castle in 1072 to secure northern England. It became the palace of Durham's powerful Prince Bishops and has housed University College since 1837.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Cross the green to a Norman giant sheltering a saint of Lindisfarne and England's first historian.
stops.Hint_1: The cathedral fills the south side of Palace Green.
stops.Hint_2: Approach its great north door; the resting places are those of Cuthbert and Bede.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Construction of Durham Cathedral began in 1093. Its innovative rib vaulting is a landmark of Norman architecture, and the church holds the shrine of St Cuthbert and the tomb of the Venerable Bede.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Finish in the year 1899, where a queen's name guards snug rooms, coal fires and a wooden cash drawer.
stops.Hint_1: Head east from the peninsula towards Hallgarth Street.
stops.Hint_2: Find the Grade II-listed Victoria Inn at number 86.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Route complete! The Victoria was built in 1899 and retains an exceptionally intact multi-room pub interior, including snug rooms and a Victorian cash drawer. It serves drinks and simple toasties rather than full meals, if open.
